सबसे पहले आप सभी का दिल से धन्यवाद। 🙏 Positive और negative, दोनों तरह के comments का मैं स्वागत करता हूँ और आपकी feedback को अपने लिए learning मानता हूँ।

Podcast में मैंने trading के बारे में जो बातें कही हैं, उन्हें practical तरीके से दिखाने के लिए मैंने 40 loss-making traders के साथ 30 Days Trading Challenge किया था।

इस challenge के दौरान Nifty लगभग 6% गिरा, फिर भी हमने सिर्फ buy trades लेकर और लगभग 40% winning rate के साथ कैसे profitability generate की, यह भी आपको देखने और सीखने को मिलेगा।

पूरी journey के week-by-week updates, मेरा P&L और participants के P&L Stock Niti channel पर उपलब्ध हैं। आपसे विनम्र निवेदन है कि एक बार ये videos ज़रूर देखें और फिर अपनी राय बनाएं। 🙏

मेरा अनुभव है कि शुरुआत में हम अक्सर 90% winning rate, no-loss strategy और हर trade में सही entry की तलाश करते रहते हैं। लेकिन strategy के साथ उसका logic, risk management और probability समझना भी उतना ही ज़रूरी है।

Trading हर trade जीतने का खेल नहीं है। जैसे cricket में हर खिलाड़ी हर मैच में अच्छा नहीं खेलता, फिर भी पूरी team जीत सकती है। वैसे ही trading में कुछ छोटे losses और कुछ बड़े winners मिलकर अच्छा परिणाम दे सकते हैं।

हर दिन 10–20 trades लेना ज़रूरी नहीं। महीने में सिर्फ 4–5 अच्छे setups मिलें, तब भी अपनी strategy के अनुसार trade किया जा सकता है। Less is more. दिन में पाँच कदम ऊपर चढ़कर रात में नौ कदम नीचे उतरने से हम मंज़िल तक नहीं पहुँच सकते।

मैंने podcast में अपने दिल की बात सरल भाषा में समझाने की कोशिश की है। रातों-रात पैसा बनाने की उम्मीद के बजाय realistic goals रखिए, धैर्य से सीखिए और सबसे पहले अपने capital को protect कीजिए।

The Strategy Steps: 
 
1. Identifying Institutional Interest: He looks for an initial, strong 'vertical' price move that deviates significantly from the previous consolidation phase. He interprets this first move (often a 20-25% influx) as a sign of institutional accumulation (50:41 - 51:19). 

2. Base Formation: After the initial spike, he waits for a 'base formation' or a period of consolidation. This phase is crucial because it indicates that big players are not interested in selling back at lower prices, allowing for a healthy accumulation of liquidity before the next leg up (49:01 - 50:14). 

3. Volume Imbalance Confirmation: He utilizes a custom screener that identifies 'volume spikes'—instances where current volume is 100 to 200 times higher than the 30-day average. This confirms the presence of institutional activity and separates genuine momentum from 'retail-to-retail' fights (01:01:28 - 01:02:17).

My Learning From Mr.Ravindra sirji, from the challenger session,

Waiting for the Setup
Avoid chasing suboptimal market moves.
Let the market come to you.
Treat trading like stalking prey, not gambling.

Sitting Through the Trade
Allow the position time to develop.
Avoid cutting winning trades too early.
Trust your stop-loss and take-profit targets.

Navigating Drawdowns
Accept that losing streaks happen to everyone.
Resist the urge to "revenge trade."
Protect your capital above all else

Ultimately No one cares about your feeling but Risk management is the KEY for your survival in the market and in the society...

The Strategy Steps: 
 
1. Identifying Institutional Interest: He looks for an initial, strong 'vertical' price move that deviates significantly from the previous consolidation phase. He interprets this first move (often a 20-25% influx) as a sign of institutional accumulation (50:41 - 51:19). 

2. Base Formation: After the initial spike, he waits for a 'base formation' or a period of consolidation. This phase is crucial because it indicates that big players are not interested in selling back at lower prices, allowing for a healthy accumulation of liquidity before the next leg up (49:01 - 50:14). 

3. Volume Imbalance Confirmation: He utilizes a custom screener that identifies 'volume spikes'—instances where current volume is 100 to 200 times higher than the 30-day average. This confirms the presence of institutional activity and separates genuine momentum from 'retail-to-retail' fights (01:01:28 - 01:02:17).

What you are doing through your podcast is absolutely right. Not everyone will understand your message, because understanding the stock market requires not just money, but also experience, knowledge, and the right mindset.

Those who have lost their hard-earned money in the stock market will understand the depth of your words. But those who have lost money in CE-PE options trading while chasing quick and massive profits may find it difficult to understand. Because there is a big difference between trading and gambling.

The stock market should be treated as a business, not a casino. Trading requires knowledge, discipline, risk management, and patience.

Remember:

A loss in a trade is not a failure. Failing to learn from that loss is the real mistake.

You cannot make a profit on every trade. But with the right strategy, controlled risk, and discipline, you can improve your chances of staying in the market for the long term.

🔥 Trade to Loss, Trading to Profit!

This means that an individual trade may result in a loss, but the goal of the overall trading process should be to achieve long-term profitability through discipline, consistency, and proper risk management.

Those who understand this difference have taken the first real step toward surviving and growing in the stock market. 📈💯
